dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Avoid the full-file read (or short-circuit to an exact read) when the requested range clearly lies beyond the whole-file window cap for large files.
evidence: agent_call.py:214-219 first read always requests `{"line_start": 1, "line_end": 0}` regardless of the requested range
agent_call.py:206-209 `_servable` returns False for a truncated entry unless `le and le <= entry['max']`
agent_call.py:232-233 truncated + not-servable → `return await self.wrapped.call_tool(name, tool_args, ...)` (a second read)
pai_tools.py:64 read_file caps the whole-file read at `_READ_MAX_LINES - 1` (2000 lines)
dropped.finding: The path-normalized read_file memo always issues a full-file (line_start=1,line_end=0) read on first access to any path, even when the model requested a deep sub-range of a large (> _READ_MAX_LINES=2000) file. For such a file the whole-file read is truncated at 2000 lines, `_servable` returns False for the deep range, and the memo then executes a SECOND exact-range read — so the first deep read of a large file now costs an extra ~2000-line read that is discarded, and every subsequent deep read still falls through to an exact read.
scenarios: Verifier reads lines 5000-5010 of a 10000-line file: memo reads 2000 lines (wasted) then the exact range

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Do not append the duplicate-read nudge when the fallback exact-range read returns an `Error:`-prefixed string.
evidence: agent_call.py:239: `return await self.wrapped.call_tool(name, tool_args, ctx, tool) + nudge`
agent_call.py:188-189: the exact-sig branch returns errors verbatim: `if isinstance(result, str) and result.startswith("Error:"): return result`
pai_tools.py:56/61 read_file returns `f"Error: {exc}"` strings
dropped.finding: In the truncated-cache fallback path a nudge string is appended to the wrapped tool's result unconditionally (`return await self.wrapped.call_tool(...) + nudge`), even when that result is an `Error:`-prefixed string. Elsewhere errors are explicitly not decorated/cached (see the exact-sig branch at lines 188-189). An error result for a repeat read of a truncated cached path thus gets a spurious duplicate-read nudge appended.
scenarios: A repeat read of a >2000-line file whose exact-range read hits an OSError/ValueError on a later access

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (or disambiguate via a sentinel) that an explicit REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS equal to 250 is treated as unset and may be lowered by the criteria-scaled floor.
evidence: completion.py: `if cfg.max_iterations == DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS or cfg.max_iterations < step_floor: cfg = replace(cfg, max_iterations=step_floor)`
config.py:127 `DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS = 250`
completion.py comment: `== DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS means no explicit operator step budget, so the scaled floor becomes the budget even when that LOWERS it`
dropped.finding: An operator who explicitly sets REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS to exactly 250 (the DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS value) is indistinguishable from the default, so their explicit budget is treated as 'no explicit budget' and can be silently LOWERED by the criteria-scaled floor (down to step_floor_min=48 for a tiny ticket) — contradicting the stated contract that 'an operator who explicitly sets a step budget still wins (min-only).'
scenarios: Operator exports REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=250 expecting a 250-step budget on a 2-criteria ticket; the floor drops it to 48
